In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a permanent seed bank is not a sufficient tool to restore a species rich grassland.
the permanent seed banks of species-rich chalk grassland are not very useful in order to restore this ecosystem.
a species-rich grassland is not only a mosaic of plant communities, but also of different seed banks, and the management of these grasslands has to take account of these different seed banks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the seed bank of a chalk grasslands is a very useful tool to restore the plant community but only if the management of the target area is designed with a view on improving dispersion process from a source to a target area.

the seed bank is a very useful tool for the restoration of plant communities in the long term, if the management is designed to preserve a given plant community, but it seems to be useless for the short and medium terms.
the seed bank is an important factor in the restoration of plant communities, but it is not sufficient to achieve this.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the management of species rich grasslands has to be designed to preserve a given plant community and to improve dispersion processes.
seed bank monitoring is a valuable tool in order to understand the dynamics of species-rich plant community and the role played by management regimes.
seed banks are not a panacea for the restoration of species richness.
